newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks plummet, capital markets jittery.
newsitem.headline: French stocks plummet, capital markets jittery.

text.p: French stock market futures plummeted while bond and interest rate futures came under pressure in pre-session electronic trading on Monday after the Socialist-led left won an upset parliamentary election triumph on Sunday.

The Franc fell slightly, slipping to 3.3855 per mark, its lowest level this year, compared to 3.3835 per mark late on Sunday after projections showed the Socialists would need support from the Communist Party to form a government.
June CAC-40 stock market futures opened 82 points lower at 2,475 and immediately fell further, dropping as low as 2,456, over four percent. At 0526 GMT they had recovered to 2,466.
June PIBOR and bond futures were lower, but holding above lows set last week after the left surprised investors and won the first round of voting.
June PIBOR futures started at 96.22, off 14 basis points, then traded down to 96.20, while the June notionnel contract was off 56 ticks at 127.94 after opening at 128.38.

Most analysts had said they expected the stock market to be the worst hit by a win by the left. The Socialists have said they favour European monetary union, albeit with conditions attached, but their policies are perceived by markets as less favourable to the corporate sector.
